title: Odin: Wisdom Has a Price
subtitle: Knowledge, leadership, and cost in the Prose Edda

learningObjectives.text: Explain the eye pledge in Snorri's Mimer's Well episode.
Distinguish that prose episode from Havamal's rune ordeal.

mimer.author: Snorri Sturluson
mimer.locator: Mimer's Well in Gylfaginning; local text normalized characters 72397-72633
mimer.excerpt: The owner of the well hight Mimer. He is full of wisdom, for he drinks from the well with the Gjallar-horn. Alfather once came there and asked for a drink from the well, but he did not get it before he left one of his eyes as a pledge.
mimer.note: Verbatim Rasmus B. Anderson translation excerpt; whitespace normalized.

runes.author: Anonymous Old Norse poets
runes.locator: Havamal, stanzas 139-140; local text normalized characters 102346-102711
runes.excerpt: 139. I ween that I hung | on the windy tree, Hung there for nights full nine; With the spear I was wounded, | and offered I was To Othin, myself to myself, On the tree that none | may ever know What root beneath it runs. 140. None made me happy | with loaf or horn, And there below I looked; I took up the runes, | shrieking I took them, And forthwith back I fell.
runes.note: Verbatim Henry Adams Bellows translation excerpt; whitespace normalized.

narrativeBlocks.title: An eye for a drink
narrativeBlocks.body: In Gylfaginning, Mimer's well contains wisdom. Odin receives a drink only after leaving one eye as a pledge.

narrativeBlocks.title: Snorri's account
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translated; whitespace normalized): “The owner of the well hight Mimer. He is full of wisdom, for he drinks from the well with the Gjallar-horn. Alfather once came there and asked for a drink from the well, but he did not get it before he left one of his eyes as a pledge.”

narrativeBlocks.title: A different ordeal in Havamal
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translated; whitespace normalized): “139. I ween that I hung | on the windy tree, Hung there for nights full nine; With the spear I was wounded, | and offered I was To Othin, myself to myself, On the tree that none | may ever know What root beneath it runs. 140. None made me happy | with loaf or horn, And there below I looked; I took up the runes, | shrieking I took them, And forthwith back I fell.”

narrativeBlocks.title: Keep the episodes separate
narrativeBlocks.body: The prose account concerns Mimer's well; Havamal 139-140 describes Odin hanging, being wounded, and taking up runes. These are distinct literary episodes.

narrativeBlocks.title: Wisdom has a cost
narrativeBlocks.body: Both texts link knowledge with sacrifice, but their shared theme does not make their episodes the same event or a record of one historical rite.

quiz.prompt: What does Odin pledge at Mimer's well in Gylfaginning?
quiz.explanation: Snorri says Mimer grants the drink after Odin leaves one eye as a pledge.
